newsitem.title: PERU: MRTA chief says rebels want to stay in Peru.
newsitem.headline: MRTA chief says rebels want to stay in Peru.

text.p: The leader of Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) said on Tuesday rebel hostage- takers wanted to stay in Peru rather than take asylum in a foreign country.

"Our first priority is to stay in our fatherland, which is the path we have chosen to fight at the side of our people," Nestor Cerpa said in a walkie-talkie conversation from within the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
Cerpa specifically ruled out an asylum deal involving the Dominican Republic, but drew short of rejecting Cuban leader Fidel Castro's offer of refuge made Monday.

"In this sense, we are clear and adamant. We have no intention of looking for exile or asylum in the Dominican Republic and even less in any country that oppresses its people," Cerpa added in the communique that was monitored by Reuters.

"With respect to the Cuban government's willingness to take us in, we consider it appropriate not to make a comment right now to avoid our words being distorted. We do this out of respect for the Cuban government, commander Fidel Castro, his revolution and his people."
The MRTA, which takes its inspiration from the 1959 Cuban revoluton, was holding 72 hostages for a 77th day Tuesday at the Japanese diplomatic compound in Lima.
